questions.stem: When gamma radiation is emitted from a nucleus, what happens to the mass number and atomic number?

options.text: Mass number decreases by 1, atomic number stays the same
Both mass number and atomic number decrease by 1
Both mass number and atomic number stay the same
Mass number stays the same, atomic number increases by 1

questions.explanation: Gamma emission involves the release of a high-energy electromagnetic wave (photon) from the nucleus. Since a gamma ray has no mass and no charge, the mass number and atomic number of the nucleus remain unchanged. The nucleus simply moves to a lower energy state.
